title: Equations with fractions, decimals and variables on both sides
blurb: Clear fractions and decimals, collect variables from both sides and recognize equations with no solution or infinitely many.
question: Priya can buy a $36 parking permit for her clinical site and then pay $2.50 a day, or skip the permit and pay $5.50 a day. The TEAS asks after how many days the two options cost the same. How do you set up and solve an equation with the variable on both sides?

teach.body: Formally, these are still linear equations in one variable: the variable appears only to the first power, and solving means finding the value that makes both sides equal. What changes is the clutter: fractions, decimals, or the variable on both sides. In plain English: tidy the equation into the simple form ax + b = c first, then solve it the usual way. Every tidying move must be done to every term on both sides.

teach.h: What makes it harder, and the fix

children.label: Fractions
children.sub: Multiply EVERY term by the LCD

children.label: Decimals
children.sub: Multiply every term by 10 or 100, or use the calculator

children.label: x on both sides
children.sub: Subtract the smaller x-term from both sides

teach.caption: After the fix, you are back to ax + b = c: undo the addition, then divide.

items: x/5 + 3 = 7. Subtract 3: x/5 = 4. Multiply both sides by 5: x = 20. Check: 20 ÷ 5 + 3 = 4 + 3 = 7. ✓
(2/3)x = 14. To undo 'times 2/3', multiply by the reciprocal 3/2: x = 14 × 3/2 = 42/2 = 21.

teach.h: Worked example: two fractions, x/4 + x/6 = 10
items: The LCD of 4 and 6 is 12. Multiply EVERY term by 12, including the 10.
Combine like terms: 5x = 120. Divide by 5: x = 24.

teach.text: Clearing fractions means multiplying EVERY term, whole numbers included. Multiply only the fractions in x/4 + x/6 = 10 and you get 3x + 2x = 10, so x = 2, a ready-made distractor. The same goes for (2/3)x = 14: multiplying by 2/3 instead of its reciprocal gives 9.33.

items: Option A: $36 permit + $2.50 per day = 36 + 2.5d. Option B: $5.50 per day = 5.5d.
Check both plans at 12 days: 36 + 2.5(12) = 36 + 30 = 66, and 5.5(12) = 66. ✓ The costs match after 12 days.

teach.h: One solution, none or infinitely many
head: Equation
After simplifying
Result
teach.caption: If the x-terms cancel, read what is left: a false statement means no solution; a true one means every number works.

items: Fractions: multiply every term by the LCD. One fraction coefficient: multiply by its reciprocal.
Decimals: solve with the calculator, or multiply every term by 10 or 100 first.
Variables on both sides: subtract one x-term from both sides, then solve as usual.
If x cancels: a false statement means no solution; a true statement means infinitely many.
Always check in the original equation.

summary: You can now clear fractions with the LCD or a reciprocal, handle decimal coefficients, and solve equations with the variable on both sides, such as finding when two pricing plans cost the same. You can also tell when an equation has no solution or infinitely many.

A.why: Multiply both sides by the reciprocal 4/3: x = 18 × 4/3 = 72/3 = 24. Check: (3/4)(24) = 72/4 = 18. ✓

whyNot.0: 13.5 multiplies 18 by 3/4 instead of by its reciprocal.
whyNot.2: 72 multiplies by 4 but forgets to divide by 3.
whyNot.3: 6 divides by 3 but forgets to multiply by 4.

whyNot.2: 0.9 divides 5.4 by 6 instead of 0.6, a decimal-place slip.
whyNot.3: 5.4 is the value of 0.6x, one step short of x.

A.why: Subtract 5x: 3x − 3 = 21. Add 3: 3x = 24. Divide: x = 8. Check: 8(8) − 3 = 61 and 5(8) + 21 = 61. ✓

whyNot.0: 6 subtracts 3 from 21 instead of adding it: 3x = 18.
whyNot.1: 24 is the value of 3x, one step short of x.
whyNot.2: −8 moves the numbers with the wrong signs, giving 3x = −24.

B.why: Multiply every term by the LCD, 12: 4x + 3x = 168, so 7x = 168 and x = 24. Check: 24 ÷ 3 + 24 ÷ 4 = 8 + 6 = 14. ✓

whyNot.0: 2 multiplies only the fractions by 12 and leaves 14 unchanged: 7x = 14.
whyNot.1: 49 adds the fractions by adding tops and bottoms (2x/7 = 14). Fractions need a common denominator.
whyNot.3: 168 is the value of 7x, one step short of x.

B.why: Multiply both sides by 5: x − 4 = 15. Add 4: x = 19. Check: (19 − 4) ÷ 5 = 15 ÷ 5 = 3. ✓

whyNot.0: 11 subtracts 4 instead of adding it: x = 15 − 4.
whyNot.2: 4.6 divides 3 by 5 instead of multiplying, then adds 4.
whyNot.3: 7 never undoes the division by 5: it treats x − 4 as 3, so x = 3 + 4.

B.q: Gym A charges $40 to join plus $25 a month. Gym B charges $10 to join plus $31 a month. After how many months will the total costs be equal? Round to the nearest tenth if needed.

whyNot.0: 8.3 adds the two joining fees (50 ÷ 6) instead of finding their difference.
whyNot.1: 0.5 adds the monthly rates (30 ÷ 56) instead of finding their difference.
whyNot.2: 1.2 divides the fee difference by Gym A's monthly rate (30 ÷ 25) instead of the difference in rates.

C.why: Distribute: 0.15x + 3 = 0.05x + 7. Subtract 0.05x: 0.1x + 3 = 7. Subtract 3: 0.1x = 4. Divide: x = 40. Check: 0.15(60) = 9 and 0.05(40) + 7 = 9. ✓

whyNot.1: 20 adds 0.05x to the left instead of subtracting it, giving 0.2x = 4.
whyNot.3: 0.4 multiplies 4 by 0.1 instead of dividing by it.

C.why: Cross-multiply: 2(2x + 1) = 3(x + 5), so 4x + 2 = 3x + 15 and x = 13. Check: 27 ÷ 3 = 9 and 18 ÷ 2 = 9. ✓

whyNot.1: 4 multiplies only the first term on each side (4x + 1 = 3x + 5).
whyNot.2: 17 adds the 2 to 15 instead of subtracting it.
whyNot.3: 3 distributes on the left but not the right (4x + 2 = 3x + 5).

C.why: 3(x + 2) = 3x + 6, so 3x + 6 = 3x + 5 simplifies to 6 = 5, which is never true: no solution.

whyNot.1: 3x + 6 = 3x + 6 simplifies to 6 = 6, which is always true: infinitely many solutions.
whyNot.2: 3x + 6 = 2x + 6 gives x = 0. Zero is a real solution, not 'no solution'.
whyNot.3: 3x + 6 = 6x + 3 gives 3 = 3x, so x = 1: exactly one solution.

reteach.title: Two bank accounts racing
reteach.question: Two friends save money: one starts with more but saves less each week, the other starts with less but saves more. When will their balances match? Why is that a 'variables on both sides' equation?

blocks.body: Aaliyah starts with $36 and adds $2.50 a week; Ben starts with $0 and adds $5.50 a week. Each balance is an expression with w in it, so 'equal balances' puts w on both sides: 36 + 2.5w = 5.5w. Ben gains $3 a week on Aaliyah (5.5 − 2.5), and he has $36 to catch up, so it takes 36 ÷ 3 = 12 weeks. That is exactly what subtracting 2.5w from both sides does.

blocks.caption: The lines cross at 12 weeks, when both balances are $66.

blocks.text: Catch-up time = head start ÷ difference in rates. Dividing by the SUM of the rates, or by one rate alone, gives the wrong answer.

explain.body: To undo multiplying by a fraction, multiply both sides by its reciprocal (flip it). For (2/5)x = 12, multiply by 5/2: x = 12 × 5 ÷ 2 = 30.

test.why: Multiply by the reciprocal 5/2: 12 × 5 = 60 and 60 ÷ 2 = 30. Check: (2/5)(30) = 60/5 = 12. ✓

whyNot.0: 4.8 multiplies by 2/5 instead of its reciprocal.
whyNot.1: 60 multiplies by 5 but forgets to divide by 2.
whyNot.2: 6 divides by 2 but forgets to multiply by 5.

explain.body: With several fractions, multiply EVERY term (whole numbers too) by the least common denominator. The fractions vanish, leaving a plain equation.

test.q: Solve for x: x/2 − x/5 = 6. Round to the nearest tenth if needed.
test.why: Multiply every term by 10: 5x − 2x = 60, so 3x = 60 and x = 20. Check: 20 ÷ 2 − 20 ÷ 5 = 10 − 4 = 6. ✓

whyNot.0: 2 multiplies only the fractions by 10 and leaves 6 unchanged: 3x = 6.
whyNot.2: 60 is the value of 3x, one step short of x.

explain.body: Treat decimals like whole numbers: undo the addition, then divide, using the calculator. Or multiply every term by 10 or 100 to clear them. Watch the decimal point when dividing.

whyNot.0: 0.4 is a decimal-place slip: 6 ÷ 1.5 is 4, not 0.4.

explain.body: Subtract one x-term from both sides so the variable appears once, then move the numbers and divide. Keep the signs attached to their terms.

test.why: Subtract 5x: 4x + 4 = −12. Subtract 4: 4x = −16. Divide: x = −4. Check: 9(−4) + 4 = −32 and 5(−4) − 12 = −32. ✓

whyNot.2: −2 adds 4 to −12 instead of subtracting it: 4x = −8.
whyNot.3: 2 treats the right side as +12 and subtracts 4: 4x = 8.
